$comment: Gemfall beat 2, The Fork. Story: docs/campaigns/gemfall.md §2. Wiring: docs/campaigns/gemfall-authoring.md. Must set on every path to every ending: exactly one of sprites_friends / sprites_wronged (decided on the branch that resolves the Harvest Stone, below choice_harvest_stone, which every path passes through) and exactly one of route_river / route_rush / route_wild (on the three choices out of choice_rumour_board into the three endings). Expanded for pacing: every path walks the stopped song, Hob's verse, the egg stall, the plank bridge, the night shiver, the corner row, the hedgehog signpost, Pib's gift and Marda's common room; none of these set route-set flags.
title: Green Roads North

plate.narration: A faun stops playing, but her watering flute keeps pouring onto her hoof. Beyond the pumpkins, wagon wheels raise a cloud of dust. A tiny sprite folds its arms. The rush is coming through somebody's garden.

objectives.label: Walked the rows instead of through them
Fed the cold wolves instead of fighting them

goal.text: Travel the Sunward Fields and choose your road north.

steps.label: Help out at the egg stall

facet_harvest.name: The Harvest Stone
facet_harvest.text: A green-gold stone from a sprites' corner row. It still wears a tiny medal: BEST.

medal_not.name: A Very Small Woven Medal
medal_not.text: Woven by harvest sprites for leaving their stone alone. It says NOT.

scene_song_stops.narration: Tonight's job: travel the Sunward Fields and choose your road north at Bramblewood. Hesper's cook packs you a supper bundle. Fauns sing in every field. Then every song stops. One faun's watering flute keeps pouring onto her own hoof.

scene_song_stops_look.narration: Down the lane rolls a cloud of dust, full of wagon wheels. Rush wagons, lots of them, and they are not slowing down. Out in the pumpkins, something tiny in an acorn helmet folds its arms.

scene_song_stops_ask.narration: You tap the faun on the shoulder. She jumps, notices her wet hoof, and turns the flute off. "Wagons," she whispers. "Rush wagons, heading for the pumpkins." Then, because you asked so nicely, she pulls a spare reed whistle out of her hat. "For when you need everybody to hear you. Just one loud note, though. It only has the one."

scene_trampled_field.narration: Rush wagons are cutting through the unpicked pumpkins to dodge a jam. A faun foreman named Hob Thistledown waves his hat. "Help me turn them, before the whole season is soup!"

scene_trampled_field_duty.narration: You plant your feet in front of the lead wagon. The oxen stop with their noses on your coat. The drover shouts. You stay. A pumpkin rolls up and stays too. The drover gives up and turns the oxen.

scene_trampled_field_roar.narration: You step into the road and roar. It is a polite roar, with a please in it. Every ox sits down at once. The drover looks at you and decides the field can keep its pumpkins.

check_reroute.prompt: Everybody dash in front of the lead oxen and steer them around the field

onSuccess.narration: You dash in front of the lead oxen, flapping your arms like a scarecrow in a gale. The oxen decide the edge of the field looks nicer, and the drover, sighing, lets them have it.

onFailure.narration: The oxen don't see you in all the dust. Three wagons cut a muddy stripe right through the squash before the rest swing around. A faun starts singing a very sad verse about it.

scene_walk_rows.narration: You follow the rows to a cart track around the field. Something in an acorn helmet pats your boot. When you look down, it is gone.

scene_caravan_turned.narration: The wagons take the edge track. Hob starts the song again with your names in it and hands out honeycake. "Crowded all the way to Bramblewood now," he says.

scene_caravan_turned_onward.narration: Hob tells you the life story of every pumpkin. The biggest one is called Gerald. At the crossroads he sniffs. "Eggs. Whatever rush folk pay, neighbors should not have to."

scene_caravan_turned_sing.narration: You sing the verse back, names and all, and get the tune wrong twice. Hob is delighted anyway. "Now you're Sunward," he says. "Any faun who hears that verse will help you."

scene_egg_stall.narration: At the crossroads, a faun egg seller chalks higher prices for the rush. "Rush folk pay rush prices!" she laughs. At the back, a faun dad counts too few coins. Her hen looks offended.

check_egg_price.prompt: Work out a price that is fair to the neighbors and to the rush

onSuccess.narration: You do the sums on the back of the price board. Two prices, you decide: one for the rush, and one for neighbors. The egg faun reads it twice and laughs out loud.

onFailure.narration: You do the sums three times and get three different answers. The last one says an egg costs one duck. The hen does not like that at all.

scene_egg_price_fair.narration: Now the board says RUSH PRICE and NEIGHBOR PRICE. The dad buys his dozen, and the rush pays for its hurry. The seller chalks your names on the board, so everyone knows whom to blame.

scene_egg_price_muddle.narration: The egg seller laughs so hard she sits down on the cart. "I can't do sums either!" She sells the faun dad his eggs at last year's price, then charges the next rude wagon double. The hen approves.

scene_egg_stall_buy.narration: You pay the rush price, and your purse gets much lighter. The faun dad says thank you three times. His smallest kid ties a songbird ribbon on your sleeve. "Now you have to sing." So you do, badly.

scene_egg_stall_queue.narration: The kitsune hops on the cart. "The line starts here!" Rush folk cannot resist a line. Twelve buyers join it without knowing why. By the time they reach the front, the faun dad has his eggs at the old price.

scene_egg_stall_haggle.narration: You lean on the cart like an Exchange trader and name huge prices. The rush buyers argue, then pay. The egg seller's purse clinks when she breathes. She gives the faun dad his eggs for free, and winks at you.

scene_jackalope_road.narration: Jackalopes pack the road, ears turned toward the long grass. Usually they race wagons. Today they are watching something. Up on a ridge, a woolly knot of sheeple is watching too.

scene_flock_ridge.narration: About thirty sheeple stand in one woolly knot, all in the same seven-brimmed hat. "What do we think?" asks the middle one. "We think wolves," they answer, out of step. "In the grass." "We all saw them." "Because one of us did."

scene_flock_bigfoot.narration: Nobody bolts. The flock shuffles in and leans on the bigfoot like a warm, woolly wall. A calm flock notices things. Thirty heads turn to watch the clever one among you.

check_flock_clever.prompt: Look closely enough that a whole flock decides you are worth copying

onSuccess.narration: You crouch, and you squint, and you tilt your head. Thirty sheeple crouch, squint, and tilt their heads exactly the same way. The flock has decided you are clever. Nobody told it to. It just knows.

onFailure.narration: You crouch down. The flock watches you politely and does not crouch. Then a jackalope bursts out of the grass right beside you, and that is the end of the meeting.

scene_flock_copies.narration: The flock follows your gaze and spots two cold cinder wolves in the grass. They are watching the caravan's sausage wagon. Three sheeple follow you downhill, stopping whenever you stop.

scene_flock_scatters.narration: The flock scatters in threes, calling each other too high for you to hear. It looks like thirty sheeple yawning at the sky. Soon they are back together, pretending nothing happened. One points at the long grass. Two gray shapes lie in it.

scene_jackalope_road_fly_look.narration: From above, the long grass is a green sea. Two gray shapes lie in it like boats, with an orange glow under the fur. Mountain wolves, in farm country. One looks straight up at you.

scene_wolf_sign.narration: In the long grass: warm prints and tufts of glowing charcoal fur. Cinder wolves, far from the mountain. Two lie shivering, watching the caravan's sausage wagon like a birthday cake.

check_wolf_kind.prompt: Put down your supper bundle without looking like a snack

onSuccess.narration: The wolves eat every crumb and the sausage too, curl up into one warm gray heap with eight legs, and watch you go. They are not tame. But they will remember you.

onFailure.narration: You trip over your own supper bundle. The wolves decide you are part of the offer.

encounter_wolves.narration: Two cold cinder wolves slink onto the road, glowing faintly. They are more hungry than angry.

onVictory.narration: The wolves slink back into the grass, ears down, looking embarrassed. They are a long way from home.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves knock you flat and trot off with every sausage in the wagon. Supper is very short on sausages.

scene_plank_bridge.narration: A rush wagon has cracked the canal bridge, and hay carts are stuck on the far bank. "Fix our beam, or carry our hay!" a faun calls. "Either way, we can help you at the hedges." A duck floats past on a bale.

check_bridge_beam.prompt: Everybody lift a fence post the size of a canoe and drop it in exactly the right place

onSuccess.narration: Heave. Shove. Thump. The new beam drops into place with a sound like a door shutting. The first hay cart rolls over, and the bridge does not even creak.

onFailure.narration: Heave. Shove. Splash. The beam slides off the bank and into the canal, and floats there. The fauns look at it. Then they look at each other.

scene_bridge_mended.narration: The hay carts roll home over the new beam. A faun carves a lucky pumpkin on it. A tiny acorn-helmeted guard salutes from the grass.

scene_bridge_ferry.narration: The fauns rope the floating beam to both banks. Now it is a ferry, and every hay cart crosses. The duck rides every trip. "Bridges never go anywhere anyway," says a faun.

scene_plank_bridge_carry.narration: You save the hay and leave the bridge for later. The farmers make a line across the shallow ford. Everyone sneezes before the first bale moves.

scene_plank_bridge_shoulders.narration: The bigfoot steps into the canal and lifts the cracked plank on their shoulders. "Go on," they say. Cart after cart rolls over. The duck sits on the bigfoot's head like a hat.

scene_plank_bridge_sing.narration: You sing Hob's verse across the canal. Every faun on the far bank stops. Then they sing it back, louder, and splash over with a spare plank. The bridge is mended before the last verse. The duck nods along.

scene_embermoths.narration: At sunset the caravan camps for supper. Embermoths drift overhead by the thousand, flying south, away from the mountain. One lands in your soup. It is warm, and it is going the wrong way.

scene_embermoths_soup.narration: You fish the embermoth out with a spoon. It sits there steaming, warm as cocoa, and will not leave. At bedtime it tucks itself in beside you.

scene_embermoths_watch.narration: You lie in the grass and watch the cloud drift south for a long time. Far to the north, the mountain still glows red. Not one moth flies toward it.

scene_impossible.narration: "That's impossible," says the dragonling. "Embermoths fly toward warm. Always. Back home the grandmothers would be ringing the bells." Nobody laughs. A little moth lands on the dragonling's horn, as if to say: tell them again.

choice_night_tremor.narration: In the middle of the night, the ground shivers. Cups rattle on their hooks. The wagon bells ring once, all together. Every jackalope sits up. Then it stops. Everybody is wide awake. What do we do? Everybody vote.

check_tremor_listen.prompt: Lie very, very still and hear what the ground is saying

onSuccess.narration: You press your ear flat to the cold ground and hold your breath. Far, far away, there is a sound.

onFailure.narration: You press your ear flat to the ground and hold your breath. The only thing you can hear is the caravan cook, snoring.

scene_tremor_heard.narration: One long, low note hums deep under the fields, coming from the north. It is very old and very slow. Then it fades, and the crickets start again.

scene_tremor_snore.narration: The cook snores like a kettle, then like two kettles. The ground gives one more tiny shiver. "Pass the gravy," says the cook, fast asleep. You give up and go to sleep too.

choice_night_tremor_sleep.narration: You pull the blanket over your head. In the morning, every cup in camp has shuffled to the north side of the table, all facing the same way, as if for a better look.

choice_night_tremor_stone.narration: You take out the warm red stone. It is humming one low, old note that buzzes in your fingers. When the ground goes still, so does the stone, as if the two were talking.

choice_night_tremor_moth.narration: The little embermoth beside you wakes. Its glow pulses as slow as breathing, and each pulse brings a shiver through the blanket. When the shivers stop, it sleeps. By morning it has flown south.

scene_corner_row.narration: At the last farm, Hesper turns her caravan aside. "Choose your own road at Bramblewood. Good luck." Beside the lane, harvest sprites in acorn helmets guard one unpicked corner row. A pea-pod trumpet toots.

scene_corner_row_closer.narration: You tiptoe between the cabbages. A sprite in a bean-pole tower spots you and toots twice. The whole guard stares at you, like a librarian at someone eating chips. Then they step aside.

scene_corner_row_salute.narration: You salute. One sprite salutes so hard it falls over. Introductions include every rank and favorite vegetable. Then the guards show you the middle of the row.

scene_corner_row_wave.narration: "The bridge ones!" Tiny trumpets play. The sprites offer a bench much too small for you, then proudly show you what they guard.

choice_harvest_stone.narration: In the middle of the row sits a green-gold sky-stone wearing a woven BEST medal. "It fell here, so it belongs here," the sprites say. You could trade, earn it, leave it, or take it anyway. They will remember.

check_trade.prompt: Offer the sprites the best thing in your pockets

onSuccess.narration: You offer a shiny button, a song, and your very best joke. The sprites go into a huddle. They come out of the huddle. It's a deal.

onFailure.narration: The sprites look at your offer for a long four seconds. Then they point, all together, at the weeds in the row. They don't want things. They want help.

check_earn.prompt: Pick up every dropped seed before the sprites do

onSuccess.narration: It's a race, and it was always a race. You win by one seed. The sprites are thrilled, and tuck a honeycake into your pocket for later.

onFailure.narration: The sprites beat you to every seed, and you get stung by a nettle on the last one. But you worked till lunchtime without complaining, and the sprites decide that counts.

check_steal.prompt: Snatch the stone between one trumpet toot and the next

onSuccess.narration: Toot. Swap. Snatch. You are gone before the new guards reach their spots. Nobody saw. Probably.

onFailure.narration: You grab it, and the trumpet toots the alarm. Forty sprites riding jackalopes chase you down three rows and through a nettle patch before you get away.

scene_medal_ceremony.narration: There is an award ceremony. The best beet gets a medal. The best bean gets a medal. Then the sprites hand you the Harvest Stone, medal and all. "Keep it somewhere with a nice view."

scene_stolen.narration: The stone is in your pack. Behind you, the corner row has gone very quiet. Every sprite has stopped to look at you. Nobody says anything. Harvest sprites do not need to. Harvest sprites remember.

scene_leave_it.narration: You leave the stone exactly where it fell. The sprites look at each other. Then they hold a second, smaller ceremony and pin a very small woven medal on you. It says NOT. Nobody explains.

scene_signpost.narration: Outside Bramblewood's tall hedges stands a signpost covered in rush signs: GEMS! SHORTCUT! NO, THIS WAY! A jackalope sits on top, enjoying the view. The real sign is somewhere underneath.

check_signpost.prompt: Peel off the rush's signs without bringing the whole post down

onSuccess.narration: Board by board, you peel the rush's signs away. Underneath, carved deep and very old, is the real one.

onFailure.narration: You pull one sign too many. Every board slides off at once and lands in a heap, all pointing different ways. You pick the biggest.

scene_signpost_found.narration: The old carved sign points to Bramblewood. Another arm shows a cornfield with one corner missing. You take the quiet lane and leave the rush signs in a tidy pile.

scene_signpost_lost.narration: The biggest sign says GEMS THIS WAY. It leads to a duck pond. The ducks are not impressed. A fishing faun points you the right way, and only laughs a little. By suppertime you can see the hedges.

scene_signpost_ruts.narration: Every wagon went this way. So do you. The ruts lead straight into a crowd outside the tall hedges. You found Bramblewood. So did everybody else.

scene_signpost_cart.narration: The egg cart rattles up, and the egg seller waves you aboard. "Neighbor price. Free!" She takes a farm lane the rush has never heard of, with the hen on your lap, and drops you at the hedges.

scene_signpost_direct.narration: You climb up beside the jackalope and start pointing. Wagons this way. Walkers that way. Nobody through the fields. You look so official that everyone obeys. When you climb down, the jackalope stays up there, pointing, in charge.

scene_hedge_mob.narration: Outside Bramblewood's tall hedges, a mob of treasure hunters shouts, "Open up!" The hedges ignore them. A small thorny sprite with a huge satchel trims one leaf at a time. "I'm Pib. I keep the hedges. They only open for people who ask properly. Will you?"

scene_hedge_mob_flock.narration: You bow to the hedge. The three sheeple who followed you bow too, then call in silence. Soon thirty sheeple arrive, bowing. "Please may we come in?" they say, out of step. The mob goes quiet. The hedge opens a path wide enough for {party}, and the flock trots in too.

scene_hedge_mob_cousins.narration: Pib sees the sprites' medal and gasps. "You've met my cousins!" The hedge opens before Pib finishes the sentence. A thorn reaches out and gently straightens the little medal.

scene_hedge_mob_help_pib.narration: You each take a brush and trim with Pib, one leaf at a time. Pib narrates every leaf. Around leaf four hundred, the hedge rustles like a cat deciding to like you, and a small gap opens.

check_hedge.prompt: Say why you came, plainly enough for a hedge to hear

onSuccess.narration: The hedge rustles, thinks about it, and quietly opens a path just wide enough for you and nobody else. The mob doesn't even notice. Pib looks very proud of the hedge.

onFailure.narration: You mean it, but it comes out sounding like a speech. The hedge has heard a lot of speeches this week.

scene_long_path.narration: Pib hands you a thorn brush, and you say sorry to the hedge. It opens a path with eleven bends while it thinks it over. By the end, the crowd has shouted itself hoarse.

choice_pib_gift.narration: Inside, Pib walks you up the lane to an inn with very tall doors, then digs in the satchel. "I can only spare one gift," says Pib. "The hedge says choose together." Which one? Everybody vote.

choice_pib_gift_pin.narration: Pib pins the thistle on your coat. "Prickly," they say. "But only on the outside. Like a hedge." The thistle stands up very straight, proud to be chosen.

choice_pib_gift_feather.narration: Pib hands over a soft gray owl feather on a clasp. "The hedge kept it for somebody clever. It thinks that might be you. It isn't sure." The feather tickles, as if it is still thinking.

choice_pib_gift_pebble.narration: Pib drops a pebble with a hole in it into your hand. "When things go wrong, look through the hole, and they go a bit less wrong." Pib shows you, staring through it for a very long time.

rest_marda_inn.narration: A centaur innkeeper named Marda Thorn ducks under her own huge door and brings you stew. "Eat first," she says. "There is time." Three tables argue about the roads north. A rumor board waits under a lamp.

rest_marda_inn_show_ember.narration: Marda holds the warm red stone to her ear. The room goes quiet. The stone hums. "Mm," says Marda, and wipes her hand on her apron, as if the hum might rub off. Then she asks her question.

scene_marda_question.narration: Marda pulls up a stool, which creaks. "I ask everybody this season: where is it all going?" She doesn't mean the road. She waits for your whole answer. "Me, I believe all three rumors. That's the trouble."

choice_common_room.narration: You can only hear one table properly. A frogfolk ferrier sits by the window. A muddy relay runner sits by the fire. A rush drover eats three dinners by the door. "Whose news will you hear?" asks Marda.

choice_common_room_frog.narration: The ferrier talks slowly. West, the Whispering Marsh is busy for the first time in a hundred years. Her cousins pole travelers they like. Rude ones get left on an island to think. "If the marsh likes you, it's the gentlest road."

choice_common_room_runner.narration: The runner talks fast. East, the line at Stone Crossing is moving again. The trolls there take a story instead of coins. A river drake charges double if you won't wait. "Past the river, you see trouble coming a day away."

choice_common_room_drover.narration: The drover talks with her mouth full. North is the shortest road, and the whole rush is on it, wheel to wheel. "You don't walk the Rush Road," she says. "You fall in, and it carries you to the ford. Then you wait."

choice_common_room_tremor.narration: You tell the room about the shiver and the hum. The ferrier felt it in the reeds. The runner felt it on the road. The drover's teacups all shuffled north. Marda says nothing at all, which, from Marda, means a lot.

choice_rumour_board.narration: The rumor board shows three roads north. East, the River Road to Stone Crossing. North, the Rush Road, with everybody else. West, the Wild Road through the marsh. "Shorter is not quicker," says Marda. Which road?

end_river.narration: East, then. Marda chalks your names under EAST, and in the morning you'll take the Sunward road to the Great River, where the trolls want stories instead of coins. Tonight you sleep in a real bed.

variants.text: The job at the canal brought help all the way to the hedge.

end_rush.narration: North, then, with everybody else. Marda chalks your names at the bottom of a very long NORTH list. All night, wagons creak past the hedges, every one going your way.

variants.text: The job at the canal brought help all the way to the hedge.

end_wild.narration: West, then, where hardly anybody goes. Marda chalks your names under WEST, where there is lots of room. Out past the hedges, the marsh frogs sing, as if they know you are coming.

variants.text: The job at the canal brought help all the way to the hedge.

interaction_egg_baskets.narration: You pass the egg baskets down the line while the hen watches every shell. Not one cracks. The egg seller tucks a wrapped supper into your pack. "For the road," she says.

interaction_jackalope_hats.narration: The jackalopes will not budge. Then one with a single white ear hops under a straw hat. "Their leader," says a passing faun. "Find her, and they'll let you by." The others shuffle the hats. Watch the white ear.

interaction.cue: Watch the white ear, then pick the hat she is under.

onSuccess.narration: There she is. She thumps her foot, and the jackalopes part toward the long grass.

onFailure.narration: Wrong hat. That jackalope sneezes. The leader pops out of another one and thumps, and the crowd parts anyway.

onAssisted.narration: A faun points to the right hat. The leader thumps, and the crowd parts.

scene_mimic_ditch.narration: A long gray plank lies across the last ditch. A faun called Burdock twists his hat. "Don't step on it," he whispers. "It's a mire mimic, mud pretending to be a plank. My hay needs to cross!" The plank blinks. So does a smaller one beside it.

choices.label: Tap it with a hay fork

encounter_mimic_plank.narration: The planks sit up on a hundred muddy toes and flop about, trying to look like planks again. Get them off the hay lane.

scene_mimic_gone.narration: The planks go floppy and slide away down the ditch. Underneath is a heap of things the rush dropped: four coins and a drover's brave whistle. "Finders keepers," says Burdock. "Thank you!"

scene_mimic_squelched.narration: You land in the ditch, wearing a lot of mud. Then Burdock's forty goats arrive, bleating. The planks hate goats. They pop away down the ditch, taking whatever they sat on. Burdock hands out warm cider.

scene_ditch_hay_home.narration: The hay cart rolls over on good solid mud. On the far side, Burdock's wife has a table of warm honeycakes. "Two coins a cake," she says. "Or a thank-you, which is also nice."

scene_ditch_cake.narration: The honeycake is so warm that it steams through your pack. Burdock's wife wraps it in a cabbage leaf and pats it twice, for luck.

interaction_moth_bells.narration: The cook hums by the fire. The last moths settle on the wagon bells and fold their wings. The camp grows dark and cozy.

interaction_stuck_wagon.narration: Near the hedges, a wagon wheel is stuck deep in a rut. Its drover, a very polite centaur, waves you over. "Steer the pole and push, and I will pull. I tip well."

interaction.cue: Friends push the wagon while someone steers the pole.

onSuccess.narration: With a slurp, the wheel pops free. The drover counts three coins into your hand. "Told you."

onFailure.narration: The wheel slides back in with a squelch, then pops out by itself. "Next time I'll ask the oxen," says the drover, and trots off.

onAssisted.narration: The drover pulls extra hard, and the wheel pops out. She counts three coins into your hand.

interaction_egg_prices.narration: The egg seller shows you her costs and the old neighbor price. Work it out together: keep the neighbor price, and give the rush its own line. The hen stands on the chalk.

interaction.cue: Share the price clues and build the two-price board.
clues: Check the cost before setting either price.
Keep the neighbor price after checking the cost.
Put the separate rush price on the board last.

onSuccess.narration: Two prices: one for the rush, and one for neighbors. The egg seller reads it twice and laughs out loud.

onFailure.narration: Three tries, three answers. The last one says an egg costs one duck. The hen does not like that at all.

onAssisted.narration: The egg seller checks each line beside you. Together you finish the two-price board.

interaction_bridge_load.narration: The fauns show you how to level a long beam, then set it in. "We'll lend you our brace at the hedges, if you need it," they say. The duck inspects both banks.

interaction.cue: Level the beam, then carry it into the bridge supports.

onSuccess.narration: Heave. Shove. Thump. The beam drops into place, and the first hay cart rolls over without a creak.

onFailure.narration: Heave. Shove. Splash. The beam slides into the canal and floats there. The fauns look at each other.

onAssisted.narration: A faun steadies one end while you level the beam. Together you set it in place.

interaction_hay_line.narration: Pass each bale toward the barn. On your own, toss it to the waiting farmer. "Get our hay home and we'll bring our brushes to the hedges," the crew promises. The duck wants a turn.

interaction.cue: Catch the hay bale and pass it toward the barn.

onSuccess.narration: The hay reaches the barn. The farmers pack their brushes for the hedges.

onFailure.narration: The farmers catch the slipping bale. They finish the last cart while you go on.

onAssisted.narration: A farmer fills a gap beside you. The hay gets home, and the crew brings its brushes.

interaction_hedge_brace.narration: The fauns from the canal bridge catch up with their long brace pole. "You helped our bridge," they say. One branch is tangled. Hold the brace steady while Pib frees it. Alone, lean it on the prop post.

interaction.cue: Hold the borrowed brace while the branch is guided aside.

onSuccess.narration: Pib frees the branch, and the hedge opens. The fauns take their brace home.

onFailure.narration: The branch slips back. Pib leads you the long way while the hedge untangles itself.

onAssisted.narration: Pib props the brace beside you. Together you free the branch.

scene_hay_crew_hedge.narration: The hay crew arrives with long-handled brushes, just as they promised. Pib directs the work, leaf by leaf, while you clear the cuttings. A small path opens, and the farmers wave you through.

interaction_hedge_request.narration: Pib makes a quiet space by the hedge. Take turns: ask to come in, say why you travel, or offer to help. The hedge waits for the whole answer. One leaf leans closer.

interaction_hedge_request_response_ask.narration: The hedge gives a thoughtful rustle. Pib repeats your request gently. A path opens at your height.

interaction_hedge_request_response_reaso.narration: The hedge listens to your whole answer. Pib repeats it gently. A path opens at your height.

interaction_hedge_request_response_help.narration: Pib names a small job, and the leaf leans closer. Pib helps you ask one part at a time, until the hedge listens.

voiceGuide.tone: warm green farm country with something wrong at the edges; funny, kind, a little uneasy, never scary
forbidden: explaining why the embermoths are flying the wrong way
naming a sheeple, or showing fewer than three

npcVoices.hob: Hob Thistledown, a faun field foreman; warm and half-singing, turns every answer into an anecdote, waves his hat a lot
npcVoices.sprites: harvest sprites; tiny, earnest, over-explaining, very serious about guard duty and award ceremonies, heartbroken by a refusal for about four seconds
npcVoices.pib: a bramble sprite the size of a teapot who keeps the hedges; earnest, narrates their own maintenance, offers you things you did not ask for, cannot open the hedges for anyone who has not asked properly
npcVoices.marda: Marda Thorn, a gray-dappled centaur innkeeper; unhurried, asks one question and waits for the whole answer, never repeats herself
npcVoices.drover: a grumpy rush-caravan drover in a hurry who is, underneath, fond of her dinner
npcVoices.sheeple: a flock of sheeple, never fewer than three and never named; warm, agreeable, and in chorus, checks with the others first ("What do we think?"), answers in three voices slightly out of step, finishes each other's sentences, skittish but never silly
npcVoices.flute_faun: the faun with the irrigation flute; startled, whispery, generous to anyone polite
npcVoices.egg_faun: a faun egg-seller at the crossroads; laughs easily, cannot do sums, fierce about neighbors paying neighbor prices
npcVoices.cook: the caravan cook; only ever talks in her sleep, about gravy
npcVoices.ferrier: a frogfolk ferrier with reeds in her hat; slow, storytelling, fond of the marsh and politely firm about rude passengers
npcVoices.relay_runner: a muddy centaur relay runner; talks fast, plain, practical, has seen the whole road east

interaction_egg_baskets.narration: Neighbors arrive with baskets. Catch and pass the eggs down the line while the seller counts them out. The hen supervises every shell.

interaction.cue: Catch the basket, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: Not one egg cracks. The last basket reaches the faun dad at the back, and he is grinning from ear to ear. The egg faun tucks a wrapped supper into your pack. "Bread, cheese and a bit of everything," she says. "For the road."

onFailure.narration: One egg rolls off the cart, and the hen catches it in her wing, which nobody knew she could do. "Professional," says the egg faun. The line goes on.

onAssisted.narration: The egg faun passes half the baskets herself, and between you not one egg cracks. She tucks a wrapped supper into your pack. "Bread, cheese and a bit of everything," she says. "For the road."

interaction_moth_bells.narration: Straggler moths glow on the wagon bells in a pattern. Echo their lullaby. The cook waits with her ladle raised. She would like to go to bed too.

interaction.cue: Watch the bells glow, then ring them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: Ding, dong, dong, clang. The stragglers sigh in a glowing sort of way and tuck their wings in. The camp goes dark and cozy, and everybody falls asleep fast.

onFailure.narration: Ding, clang, dong. The moths flicker crossly, then give up and settle down anyway. The camp goes dark and cozy, and everybody falls asleep fast.

onAssisted.narration: The cook hums the lullaby under her breath, and you ring along. The stragglers sigh and tuck their wings in, and everybody falls asleep fast.

interaction_hedge_request.narration: Pib makes a quiet space by the hedge. Each hero asks to come in, says why you are traveling, or offers to help. The hedge waits for the whole answer. One leaf leans closer than the others.

interaction.cue: Each hero helps ask the hedge politely.

options.label: Ask to come in
options.reaction: Your request gets a thoughtful rustle.

options.label: Explain why I am traveling
options.reaction: The hedge listens without interrupting your answer.

options.label: Offer Pib some help
options.reaction: Pib names a small job, and the listening leaf leans closer.

onSuccess.narration: Pib repeats your request gently. The hedge opens a path at your height.

onFailure.narration: You mean it, but it comes out sounding like a speech. The hedge has heard a lot of speeches this week.

onAssisted.narration: Pib helps you ask one part at a time. Together you find words the hedge will listen to.
